supersedes.reason: v1 g15 asserted that upper-case hex digits decode (same bytes, same hash, lower-case output). DE-91 and DECISION.md section 2 (execution.calldata) say calldata is 0x plus LOWER-CASE hex of whole bytes, never upper case, so the decoder was more lenient than the specification and the Console review screen and the signer could disagree about what a calldata text means (finding DAXCORE1-F2, DAX7C-F4). The specification is the authority: v2 g15 is the calldata_hex_invalid case and the decoder refuses every non-lower-case digit itself. v1 stays on disk, unedited and sha256 pinned, as history; its g15 is the superseded case and is no longer run as a decode.

note: FICTIONAL parties and tokens only. Expected outputs are written by an independent generator (own ABI encoder, own formatter by division and remainder, own sentence templates, keccak from the signer implementation), not produced by packages/core. VERSION 2 (DAX-CORE-2, ruling R1 = OQ-CORE1-3): identical to v1 in the registry, the registryCanonical, the registryHash and 49 of the 50 cases; the ONE superseded case is g15.
